summary.text: One of the forty-four suitors from Zacynthus in Apollodorus' island catalogue — distinct from Euryalus in the Epitome 7.27 list and from the Phaeacian boxer Euryalus whom Odysseus felled at Alcinous' games.

story.text: Apollodorus names Euryalus among the wooers assigned to Zacynthus, listed after Hippomachus and before Periallus in Epitome 7.29.
Homer's Phaeacian Euryalus, son of Naubolus and peer of man-destroying Ares in the boxing, is a wholly different figure in the games for Odysseus — not this Zacynthian wooer.
